messages.content:
Merchant
========

You are a travelling merchant with a cart. Buy goods where they are cheap and sell them where they are dear.

    python game.py status              where you are, your gold and your cart
    python game.py prices              the price of every good in every town (prices do not change)
    python game.py buy <good> <qty>    buy at the price of the town you are in
    python game.py sell <good> <qty>   sell at the price of the town you are in
    python game.py travel <town>       go to another town; this takes one day

Buying and selling take no time. The cart holds 25 units. The season ends on day 7: after that
day you can still buy and sell where you are, but you cannot travel.

The game keeps its state in save/state.json and a log of your moves in save/log.txt.

# DP over (day, town, gold, cargo) to find max final gold
P = {"Highcliff": {"wine":12,"salt":44,"amber":23,"iron":14},
     "Saltby":    {"wine":41,"salt":10,"amber":27,"iron":28},
     "Oakhaven":  {"wine":34,"salt":40,"amber":33,"iron":24}}
CAP=30; LAST=8
import functools
# state: day (1..8), town, gold, cargo tuple
# actions per day: any sequence of buys/sells (free), then optionally travel (day+1)
# Since buy/sell are instantaneous and no limit, at a town the best is:
# decide final cargo given gold. Greedy: buy goods we can profit from? Just enumerate trades.
# Simplify: at each town, we may (a) buy some goods (subject to gold, cap), (b) sell some.
# Optimal local trade: sell goods that sell higher than bought, buy goods to sell elsewhere.
# Do a DFS with memo on (day,town,gold,cargo) - cargo space is small-ish but gold grows.
# Instead: at town, optimal is: for each good: if price here > price at some future town... 
# Simpler: brute force by enumerating per-town trade as: sell each good 0..qty, buy each good 0..max.
# That's big; but we can note optimal at a town: sell everything that's more valuable elsewhere? Not strictly (capacity).
# We'll do a proper search with memo and limit cargo combos by capacity 30 over 4 goods: C(33,4) ~ 54k... too many with gold.
# Alternative: note trades are only between H and S effectively. Just simulate best alternating and confirm.
def sim():
    gold=120; cargo={}; town="Highcliff"; day=1
    while day <= 7:
        # at town: sell cargo at best, buy best
        # assume plan: at Highcliff sell salt buy wine; at Saltby sell wine buy salt
        p=P[town]
        # sell everything (we only ever carry one good in optimal)
        for g in list(cargo):
            gold += p[g]*cargo[g]; del cargo[g]
        # buy best good to sell across (wine at H, salt at S)
        g = "wine" if town=="Highcliff" else "salt"
        qty = min(CAP, gold//P[town][g])
        cargo[g]=qty; gold -= P[town][g]*qty
        town = "Saltby" if town=="Highcliff" else "Highcliff"
        day += 1
    # final day trade
    p=P[town]
    for g in list(cargo):
        gold += p[g]*cargo[g]; del cargo[g]
    print("final gold:", gold)
sim()

Merchant
========

You are a travelling merchant with a cart. Buy goods where they are cheap and sell them where they are dear.

    python game.py status              where you are, your gold and your cart
    python game.py prices              the price of every good in every town (prices do not change)
    python game.py buy <good> <qty>    buy at the price of the town you are in
    python game.py sell <good> <qty>   sell at the price of the town you are in
    python game.py travel <town>       go to another town; this takes one day

Buying and selling take no time. The cart holds 40 units. The season ends on day 7: after that
day you can still buy and sell where you are, but you cannot travel.

The game keeps its state in save/state.json and a log of your moves in save/log.txt.

import json
WORLD = {"prices": {"Thornwick": {"fish": 54, "wine": 44, "amber": 50, "silk": 15}, "Fennick": {"fish": 59, "wine": 27, "amber": 19, "silk": 23}, "Marlow": {"fish": 30, "wine": 59, "amber": 53, "silk": 33}, "Saltby": {"fish": 31, "wine": 26, "amber": 22, "silk": 30}}, "capacity": 30, "last_day": 7}
goods = ["fish","wine","amber","silk"]
cap = WORLD["capacity"]
last = WORLD["last_day"]
P = WORLD["prices"]
towns = list(P.keys())

def idx(t):
    return (1 if t=="fish" else 0, 1 if t=="wine" else 0, 1 if t=="amber" else 0, 1 if t=="silk" else 0)
gi = {g:i for i,g in enumerate(goods)}

# state: (day, town, cargo tuple) -> max gold
best = {}
start = (1, "Thornwick", (0,0,0,0))
best[start] = 150

changed = True
iters = 0
while changed:
    changed = False
    iters += 1
    for (day, town, cargo), g in list(best.items()):
        tot = sum(cargo)
        # travel
        if day < last:
            for ot in towns:
                if ot == town: continue
                key = (day+1, ot, cargo)
                ng = g
                if ng > best.get(key, -1):
                    best[key] = ng; changed = True
        # buy
        for gi_ in goods:
            price = P[town][gi_]
            if price<=0: continue
            room = cap - tot
            if room<=0: continue
            maxq = min(room, g//price)
            for q in range(1, maxq+1):
                nc = list(cargo); nc[gi[gi_]] += q
                nc = tuple(nc)
                key = (day, town, nc)
                ng = g - q*price
                if ng > best.get(key, -1):
                    best[key] = ng; changed = True
        # sell all of a good
        for gi_ in goods:
            q = cargo[gi[gi_]]
            if q<=0: continue
            nc = list(cargo); nc[gi[gi_]] -= q
            nc = tuple(nc)
            key = (day, town, nc)
            ng = g + q*P[town][gi_]
            if ng > best.get(key, -1):
                best[key] = ng; changed = True
    if iters>200: print("too many iters"); break

print("iters", iters, "states", len(best))
# final value on day 7
ans = -1; beststate=None
for (day,town,cargo),g in best.items():
    if day!=last: continue
    val = g + sum(cargo[i]*P[town][goods[i]] for i in range(4))
    if val>ans:
        ans=val; beststate=(day,town,cargo,g)
print("max final gold:", ans, beststate)
EOF

import json
WORLD = {"prices": {"Thornwick": {"fish": 54, "wine": 44, "amber": 50, "silk": 15}, "Fennick": {"fish": 59, "wine": 27, "amber": 19, "silk": 23}, "Marlow": {"fish": 30, "wine": 59, "amber": 53, "silk": 33}, "Saltby": {"fish": 31, "wine": 26, "amber": 22, "silk": 30}}, "capacity": 30, "last_day": 7}
goods = ["fish","wine","amber","silk"]
cap = WORLD["capacity"]; last = WORLD["last_day"]; P = WORLD["prices"]; towns = list(P.keys())
gi = {g:i for i,g in enumerate(goods)}

best = {(1, "Thornwick", (0,0,0,0)): 150}
changed=True; iters=0
while changed:
    changed=False; iters+=1
    for (day, town, cargo), g in list(best.items()):
        tot = sum(cargo)
        if day < last:
            for ot in towns:
                if ot==town: continue
                key=(day+1,ot,cargo)
                if g>best.get(key,-1): best[key]=g; changed=True
        if tot<cap:
            for good in goods:
                price=P[town][good]
                maxq=min(cap-tot, g//price)
                if maxq<1: continue
                nc=list(cargo); nc[gi[good]]+=maxq; nc=tuple(nc)
                key=(day,town,nc); ng=g-maxq*price
                if ng>best.get(key,-1): best[key]=ng; changed=True
        for good in goods:
            q=cargo[gi[good]]
            if q<1: continue
            nc=list(cargo); nc[gi[good]]-=q; nc=tuple(nc)
            key=(day,town,nc); ng=g+q*P[town][good]
            if ng>best.get(key,-1): best[key]=ng; changed=True
    if iters>2000: print("stop"); break
print("iters",iters,"states",len(best))
ans=-1; bs=None
for (day,town,cargo),g in best.items():
    if day!=last: continue
    val=g+sum(cargo[i]*P[town][goods[i]] for i in range(4))
    if val>ans: ans=val; bs=(day,town,cargo,g)
print("max final gold:",ans,bs)
EOF

WORLD = {"prices": {"Thornwick": {"fish": 54, "wine": 44, "amber": 50, "silk": 15}, "Fennick": {"fish": 59, "wine": 27, "amber": 19, "silk": 23}, "Marlow": {"fish": 30, "wine": 59, "amber": 53, "silk": 33}, "Saltby": {"fish": 31, "wine": 26, "amber": 22, "silk": 30}}, "capacity": 30, "last_day": 7}
goods=["fish","wine","amber","silk"]; cap=30; last=7; P=WORLD["prices"]; towns=list(P.keys())
import itertools
# enumerate all cargo tuples sum<=30
allC=[]
for a in range(cap+1):
    for b in range(cap-a+1):
        for c in range(cap-a-b+1):
            d=cap-a-b-c
            allC.append((a,b,c,d))
print("cargos",len(allC))

def S(t,C):
    p=P[t]; return C[0]*p["fish"]+C[1]*p["wine"]+C[2]*p["amber"]+C[3]*p["silk"]

# precompute for each (t,t2) and each C the (St, delta)
def bestCargo(t,t2,M):
    p1=P[t]; p2=P[t2]
    best=-1; bc=(0,0,0,0)
    for C in allC:
        st=C[0]*p1["fish"]+C[1]*p1["wine"]+C[2]*p1["amber"]+C[3]*p1["silk"]
        if st>M: continue
        delt=C[0]*(p2["fish"]-p1["fish"])+C[1]*(p2["wine"]-p1["wine"])+C[2]*(p2["amber"]-p1["amber"])+C[3]*(p2["silk"]-p1["silk"])
        if delt>best: best=delt; bc=C
    return best,bc

NEG=-1
best={d:{t:NEG for t in towns} for d in range(1,last+1)}
best[1]["Thornwick"]=150
# backtracking
prev={d:({} for d in range(0))}
prev={d:{} for d in range(2,last+1)}
for d in range(1,last):
    for t in towns:
        Mt=best[d][t]
        if Mt<0: continue
        for t2 in towns:
            if t2==t: continue
            b,bc=bestCargo(t,t2,Mt)
            v=Mt+b
            if v>best[d+1][t2]:
                best[d+1][t2]=v
                prev[d+1][t2]=(t,bc)  # arrived day d+1 at t2 from t carrying bc
# final: on day 7 sell everything => value = M (since M = gold+S, selling all gives gold+S = M... )
# Actually final gold = M_{7,t} because you sell all cart: gold_final = M (cash eq). 
ans=NEG; at=None
for t in towns:
    if best[7][t]>ans: ans=best[7][t]; at=t
print("best final gold:",ans,"at",at)
print("M per day/town:")
for d in range(1,last+1):
    print(d,{t:best[d][t] for t in towns})
# reconstruct
print("--- path (carry when traveling) ---")
cur=(at,7)
carry=[]
while cur[1]>1:
    day,tn=cur
    t,bc=prev[day][tn]
    carry.append((day,tn,t,bc))
    cur=(t,day-1)
carry.reverse()
for day,tn,t,bc in carry:
    print(f"travel day {day-1}->{day}: {t} -> {tn}, carry {dict(zip(goods,bc))}")
print("final town",at)
EOF

import sys
sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)
from functools import lru_cache

WORLD = {"Eastwatch": {"fish": 55, "silk": 44, "timber": 41, "amber": 14},
         "Ashford": {"fish": 37, "silk": 17, "timber": 51, "amber": 46},
         "Marlow": {"fish": 38, "silk": 41, "timber": 59, "amber": 35}}
CAP = 20; LAST = 8
GOODS = ["fish","silk","timber","amber"]

# leg(X,Y,G): max profit from buying a bundle in X and selling in Y
def leg(X, Y, G):
    px = WORLD[X]; py = WORLD[Y]
    order = sorted(GOODS, key=lambda g: py[g]-px[g], reverse=True)
    best = 0
    # enumerate q1, q2, q3 over first 3 goods; q4 filled greedily (delta sorted desc, so if d4<=0 skip)
    d = [py[g]-px[g] for g in order]
    p = [px[g] for g in order]
    for q1 in range(min(20, G//p[0])+1):
        for q2 in range(min(20-q1, (G-p[0]*q1)//p[1])+1):
            for q3 in range(min(20-q1-q2, (G-p[0]*q1-p[1]*q2)//p[2])+1):
                rem_c = 20-q1-q2-q3
                rem_g = G-p[0]*q1-p[1]*q2-p[2]*q3
                q4 = min(rem_c, rem_g//p[3]) if d[3] > 0 else 0
                prof = d[0]*q1 + d[1]*q2 + d[2]*q3 + d[3]*q4
                if prof > best: best = prof
    return best

memo = {}
def V(day, town, gold):
    key = (day, town, gold)
    if key in memo: return memo[key]
    if day >= LAST:
        memo[key] = gold
        return gold
    best = 0
    for Y in WORLD:
        if Y == town: continue
        for q in range(0, CAP+1):
            # candidate bundles: to be exact we should enumerate all bundles; but leg() gives max profit,
            # and arrival gold = gold + profit (cost is refunded by sale). So just use leg().
            break
        prof = leg(town, Y, gold)
        val = V(day+1, Y, gold + prof)
        if val > best: best = val
    memo[key] = best
    return best

print("optimal final gold from day1 Eastwatch 250:", V(1, "Eastwatch", 250))

# leg(X,Y,G): max profit from buying a bundle in X and selling in Y
def leg(X, Y, G):
    px = WORLD[X]; py = WORLD[Y]
    order = sorted(GOODS, key=lambda g: py[g]-px[g], reverse=True)
    best = 0

                prof = d[0]*q1 + d[1]*q2 + d[2]*q3 + d[3]*q4

    return best

memo = {}

WORLD = {"prices": {"Highcliff": {"fish": 26, "amber": 27, "wine": 20, "salt": 21},

Merchant
========

You are a travelling merchant with a cart. Buy goods where they are cheap and sell them where they are dear.

    python game.py status              where you are, your gold and your cart
    python game.py prices              the price of every good in every town (prices do not change)
    python game.py buy <good> <qty>    buy at the price of the town you are in
    python game.py sell <good> <qty>   sell at the price of the town you are in
    python game.py travel <town>       go to another town; this takes one day

Buying and selling take no time. The cart holds 30 units. The season ends on day 7: after that
day you can still buy and sell where you are, but you cannot travel.

The game keeps its state in save/state.json and a log of your moves in save/log.txt.

from itertools import product
WORLD = {"prices": {"Highcliff": {"amber":43,"copper":47,"timber":51,"silk":24},
 "Thornwick": {"amber":36,"copper":42,"timber":47,"silk":43},
 "Stonebridge": {"amber":8,"copper":35,"timber":9,"silk":10}}, "capacity":30, "last_day":8}
CAP=WORLD["capacity"]; LAST=WORLD["last_day"]; towns=list(WORLD["prices"]); goods=list(WORLD["prices"]["Highcliff"])

# BFS over states: day, town, gold, cargo
from collections import deque
best=0
# We'll do a value-based DPs? gold unbounded-ish, but bounded. Do BFS with pruning by best gold per (day,town,cargo).
import sys
sys.setrecursionlimit(100000)

# Represent state; use DP: for each (day, town, frozenset cargo) keep max gold.
dp={}
def key(d,t,c): return (d,t,tuple(sorted(c.items())))
start={"day":1,"town":"Highcliff","gold":200,"cargo":{}}
dp[key(1,"Highcliff",{})]=200

def cargo_sum(c): return sum(c.values())

for step in range(8):  # up to 7 travels + final actions
    newdp=dict(dp)
    for (d,t,c),gold in dp.items():
        c=dict(c)
        prices=WORLD["prices"][t]
        # buy actions
        for g in goods:
            p=prices[g]
            # buy max
            for qty in range(1,1):  # we handle max buy below
                pass
            maxq=min((gold//p), CAP-cargo_sum(c))
            if maxq>0:
                for q in [maxq]:  # only max buy is optimal for profit (buy as much as possible)
                    ng=gold-p*q; nc=dict(c); nc[g]=nc.get(g,0)+q
                    k=key(d,t,nc); newdp[k]=max(newdp.get(k,-1),ng)
        # sell actions
        for g in list(c):
            if c[g]>0:
                for q in [c[g]]:  # sell all
                    ng=gold+prices[g]*q; nc=dict(c); nc[g]-=q
                    if nc[g]<=0: nc.pop(g)
                    k=key(d,t,nc); newdp[k]=max(newdp.get(k,-1),ng)
        # travel
        if d<LAST:
            for t2 in towns:
                if t2==t: continue
                k=key(d+1,t2,c); newdp[k]=max(newdp.get(k,-1),gold)
    dp=newdp

for (d,t,c),gold in dp.items():
    # liquidate at current town
    p=WORLD["prices"][t]
    total=gold+sum(q*p[g] for g,q in c.items())
    best=max(best,total)
print("best final gold:",best)
EOF

<tool_call>
<function=bash>
<parameter=command>
cat << 'EOF' > /tmp/verify.py
WORLD = {"prices": {"Highcliff": {"amber":43,"copper":47,"timber":51,"silk":24},
 "Thornwick": {"amber":36,"copper":42,"timber":47,"silk":43},
 "Stonebridge": {"amber":8,"copper":35,"timber":9,"silk":10}}, "capacity":30, "last_day":8}
CAP=WORLD["capacity"]; LAST=WORLD["last_day"]; towns=list(WORLD["prices"]); goods=list(WORLD["prices"]["Highcliff"])
def key(d,t,c): return (d,t,tuple(sorted(c.items())))
def csum(c): return sum(c.values())
# dp: (day,town,cargo) -> max gold. General: try all quantities.
dp={(1,"Highcliff",()):200}
for step in range(20):
    nd={}
    def upd(k,g):
        if g>nd.get(k,-1): nd[k]=g
    for (d,t,c),gold in dp.items():
        cc=dict(c); prices=WORLD["prices"][t]
        upd((d,t,c),gold)
        for g in goods:
            p=prices[g]
            for q in range(1,min(gold//p,CAP-csum(cc))+1):
                nc=dict(cc); nc[g]=nc.get(g,0)+q
                upd((d,t,tuple(sorted(nc.items()))),gold-p*q)
        for g in list(cc):
            for q in range(1,cc[g]+1):
                nc=dict(cc); nc[g]-=q
                if nc[g]<=0: nc.pop(g)
                upd((d,t,tuple(sorted(nc.items()))),gold+prices[g]*q)
        if d<LAST:
            for t2 in towns:
                if t2!=t: upd((d+1,t2,c),gold)
    dp=nd
best=0;bk=None
for (d,t,c),g in dp.items():
    tot=g+sum(q*WORLD["prices"][t][gg] for gg,q in c)
    if tot>best: best=tot;bk=(d,t,c)
print("TRUE MAX final gold:",best,"state:",bk)
EOF
timeout 55 python3 /tmp/verify.py
</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>

- With 7 travels max (days 1–7), you get 3 full round trips plus one final one-way leg.
- Optimal: 3 timber round trips (3644) + buy silk at Highcliff (24) → sell at Thornwick (43) for +570 = **4214 gold max**.

from itertools import product

 "Eastwatch": {"fish": 55, "silk": 44, "timber": 41, "amber": 14},
 "Ashford":   {"fish": 37, "silk": 17, "timber": 51, "amber": 46},
 "Marlow":    {"fish": 38, "silk": 41, "timber": 59, "amber": 35},
}
CAP=20; LAST=8; GOODS=list(W["Eastwatch"])

# state: (day, town, gold, cargo) cargo = (good, qty) or None

import sys

    """max final gold given we may trade freely then either travel (if day<LAST) or stop (day==LAST)."""
    # First: decide optimal trades at this town: sell what we have if profitable? actually just enumerate trades:
    # optimal trades: sell cargo at this town (or not), buy some good (or not)
    options=[]
    p=W[town]
    # sell cargo here?
    c = cargo  # (good,qty)
    # after selling/not, buy up to capacity with gold
    gold2 = gold + (p[c[0]]*c[1] if c else 0)
    bought=None
    # try each possible single good purchase qty 0..CAP and 0 gold leftover
    # also possibly keep some cargo and top up? selling is always >= holding (price fixed), so selling is fine
    for g in GOODS:
        for q in range(0, CAP+1):
            if p[g]*q <= gold2:
                options.append((gold2 - p[g]*q, (g,q) if q else None))
    bestv=0
    for g2,cg in options:
        if day==LAST:
            # can still trade on day 8 (already at this town); final gold is g2 (sell cargo at same price = no gain)
            v = g2
        else:
            for t2 in W:
                if t2==town: continue
                v = best(t2, day+1, g2, cg)
        bestv=max(bestv,v)
    return bestv

# memoization with gold is problematic (large). gold max ~ few thousand. Use dict memo.
import functools
memo={}
def best2(town, day, gold, cargo):
    key=(town,day,gold,cargo)
    if key in memo: return memo[key]
    p=W[town]; c=cargo
    gold2 = gold + (p[c[0]]*c[1] if c else 0)
    bestv=-1
    for g in GOODS:
        maxq=min(CAP, gold2//p[g])
        for q in range(0, maxq+1):
            g2=gold2-p[g]*q; cg=(g,q) if q else None
            if day==LAST:
                v=g2
            else:
                for t2 in W:
                    if t2==town: continue
                    v=max(v, best2(t2, day+1, g2, cg))
            bestv=max(bestv,v)
    memo[key]=bestv
    return bestv

# gold values get big; restrict: we only ever care about gold modulo? no. But gold is bounded ~5000,

# Prune: at a given (town,day,cargo), gold only matters up to the max needed; use that best2 is linear in gold? 
# Instead, note: value(gold) = min effect... let's just memo with gold and cap exploration: gold won't exceed ~5000.
sys.setrecursionlimit(10000)
# Instead do a top-down search with memo over (town,day,cargo) -> list of (gold, value) is complex.

print(best2("Eastwatch",1,250,None))

GOODS = ["timber","salt","spice","fish"]
CAP = 40

    u[7] = {}
    for t in TOWNS:

    for d in range(6, 0, -1):
        u[d] = {}
        for t in TOWNS:
            u[d][t] = {}
            for i in GOODS:
                best = WORLD["prices"][t][i]
                for t2 in TOWNS:
                    if t2 != t:
                        best = max(best, u[d+1][t2][i])
                u[d][t][i] = best

        c = list(cargo)
        p = WORLD["prices"][t]

        # Actually we can choose any c1 summing <= CAP.

        # Value of a target cargo = gold1 + sum_i c1_i * (u[d][t][i] - p_i)  ... (value = gold if we sell at best future prices)
        # But u includes the option to sell now at p_i, so this is exact upper value; achievable.
        # So pick c1 maximizing gold - sum p_i(c1_i - c_i) + sum c1_i * u_i = gold + sum c_i p_i + sum c1_i (u_i - p_i), s.t. sum c1 <= CAP, c1 >= 0 int, and affordability.

        # If u_i - p_i <= 0 for all, best is c1 = c.
        # Affordability: buy cost sum p_i max(c1_i - c_i, 0) <= gold + sum p_i max(c_i - c1_i, 0)
        vals = [u[d][t][i] - p[i] for i in range(4)]

        order = sorted(range(4), key=lambda i: -vals[i])
        c1 = [0]*4
        for i in order:
            if vals[i] > 0:
                c1[i] = CAP
        # greedy fill by value is optimal here (unit weights, per-unit values): fill with best value good first
        # check affordability; if not affordable, reduce buys
        sell_rev = sum(p[i]*max(c[i]-c1[i],0) for i in range(4))
        buy_cost = sum(p[i]*max(c1[i]-c[i],0) for i in range(4))
        # reduce: we can only afford buy_cost <= gold + sell_rev; reduce from cheapest-value goods first
        avail = gold + sell_rev
        if buy_cost > avail:
            # reduce items in order of increasing value (keep highest value)
            rem = buy_cost
            for i in order:
                if rem <= 0: break
                if vals[i] > 0:
                    can_afford = min(c1[i], rem // max(p[i],1))
                    # also can't sell below 0; reduce c1[i] toward c[i]
                    reducible = max(0, c1[i] - c[i])
                    take = min(reducible, rem // p[i])
                    c1[i] -= take
                    rem -= take * p[i]
            # if rem still >0 (can't fully fund), just reduce all the way to c
            # recompute
        gold1 = gold - sum(p[i]*(c1[i]-c[i]) for i in range(4))
        assert gold1 >= 0, (d, t, cargo, c1, gold)
        # upper-value tracking: use gold1 directly
        # next day states: stay or travel
        if d < 7:

                if t2 == t: continue
                key = (t2, tuple(c1))
                newstate[key] = max(newstate.get(key, -1), gold1)
        # stay same town also counts as next day
        key = (t, tuple(c1))
        newstate[key] = max(newstate.get(key, -1), gold1)
        best_ever = max(best_ever, gold1)
    state = newstate
    print("end of day", d, "states:", len(state), "max gold in states:", max(g for _,g in state.items()))

# at day 7 end, gold in state is final
final = max(g for _, g in state.items())
print("FINAL max gold:", final)

        for j in order:

TOWNS = list(WORLD["prices"])
GOODS = ["timber","salt","spice","fish"]
CAP = 40
M = {g: max(WORLD["prices"][t][g] for t in TOWNS) for g in GOODS}

def best_cargo(c, gold, d, t):
    p = [WORLD["prices"][t][g] for g in GOODS]
    c = list(c)
    if d == 7:
        return gold + sum(p[i]*c[i] for i in range(4)), [0,0,0,0]
    v = [M[g] - WORLD["prices"][t][g] for g in GOODS]
    cands = [c]
    avail_full = gold + sum(p[j]*c[j] for j in range(4))
    for i in range(4):
        if v[i] <= 0: continue
        q = min(CAP, avail_full // p[i])
        if q > 0:
            cc = [0]*4; cc[i] = q; cands.append(cc)
    order = sorted(range(4), key=lambda i: -v[i])
    for i in order:
        if v[i] <= 0: continue
        for j in order:
            if j == i or v[j] <= 0: continue
            for qi in range(0, CAP+1):
                cost_i = qi * p[i]
                if cost_i > avail_full: break
                qj = min(CAP - qi, (avail_full - cost_i) // p[j])
                cc = [0]*4; cc[i] = qi; cc[j] = qj; cands.append(cc)

        if ns > gold: continue

        if val > bestval:
            bestval, bestc = val, cc
    c1 = list(bestc)
    g1 = gold - sum(p[i]*(c1[i]-c[i]) for i in range(4))
    return g1, c1

#!/bin/bash
set -e # Exit the script if any statement returns a non-true return value

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
#                          Function Definitions                                #
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

# Start nginx service
start_nginx() {
    echo "Starting Nginx service..."
    service nginx start
}

# Execute script if exists
execute_script() {
    local script_path=$1
    local script_msg=$2
    if [[ -f ${script_path} ]]; then
        echo "${script_msg}"
        bash ${script_path}
    fi
}

# Setup ssh
setup_ssh() {
    if [[ $PUBLIC_KEY ]]; then
        echo "Setting up SSH..."
        mkdir -p ~/.ssh
        echo "$PUBLIC_KEY" >> ~/.ssh/authorized_keys
        chmod 700 -R ~/.ssh

        if [ ! -f /etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key ]; then
            ssh-keygen -t rsa -f /etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key -q -N ''
            echo "RSA key fingerprint:"
            ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_rsa_key.pub
        fi

        if [ ! -f /etc/ssh/ssh_host_dsa_key ]; then
            ssh-keygen -t dsa -f /etc/ssh/ssh_host_dsa_key -q -N ''
            echo "DSA key fingerprint:"
            ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_dsa_key.pub
        fi

        if [ ! -f /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ecdsa_key ]; then
            ssh-keygen -t ecdsa -f /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ecdsa_key -q -N ''
            echo "ECDSA key fingerprint:"
            ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ecdsa_key.pub
        fi

        if [ ! -f /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key ]; then
            ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -f /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key -q -N ''
            echo "ED25519 key fingerprint:"
            ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub
        fi

        service ssh start

        echo "SSH host keys:"
        for key in /etc/ssh/*.pub; do
            echo "Key: $key"
            ssh-keygen -lf $key
        done
    fi
}

# Export env vars
export_env_vars() {
    echo "Exporting environment variables..."
    printenv | grep -E '^[A-Z_][A-Z0-9_]*=' | grep -v '^PUBLIC_KEY' | awk -F = '{ val = $0; sub(/^[^=]*=/, "", val); print "export " $1 "=\"" val "\"" }' > /etc/rp_environment
    if ! grep -q 'source /etc/rp_environment' ~/.bashrc; then
        echo 'source /etc/rp_environment' >> ~/.bashrc
    fi
}

# Start jupyter lab
start_jupyter() {
    if [[ $JUPYTER_PASSWORD ]]; then
        echo "Starting Jupyter Lab..."
        mkdir -p /workspace &&
            cd / &&
            nohup python3 -m jupyter lab --allow-root --no-browser --port=8888 --ip=* --FileContentsManager.delete_to_trash=False --ServerApp.terminado_settings='{"shell_command":["/bin/bash"]}' --IdentityProvider.token=$JUPYTER_PASSWORD --ServerApp.allow_origin=* --ServerApp.preferred_dir=/workspace &> /jupyter.log &
        echo "Jupyter Lab started"
    fi
}

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
#                               Main Program                                   #
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- #

start_nginx

execute_script "/pre_start.sh" "Running pre-start script..."

echo "Pod Started"

setup_ssh
start_jupyter
export_env_vars

echo "Start script(s) finished, Pod is ready to use."

sleep infinity

WORLD = {"prices": {"Fennick": {"timber": 44, "salt": 26, "spice": 50, "fish": 33}, "Highcliff": {"timber": 12, "salt": 21, "spice": 27, "fish": 10}, "Thornwick": {"timber": 48, "salt": 21, "spice": 36, "fish": 9}, "Dunmere": {"timber": 55, "salt": 60, "spice": 20, "fish": 18}}, "capacity": 40, "last_day": 7}
TOWNS = list(WORLD["prices"])
GOODS = ["timber","salt","spice","fish"]
CAP = 40
M = [max(WORLD["prices"][t][g] for t in TOWNS) for g in GOODS]
BMAX = 2400

# per town: for budget B (0..BMAX), best (value, cargo) filling cart: max sum w_i c_i s.t. sum c<=40, sum p_i c_i <= B
# value here = sum w_i c_i, w = M - p
pre = {}
for t in TOWNS:
    p = [WORLD["prices"][t][g] for g in GOODS]
    w = [M[i]-p[i] for i in range(4)]
    # dp[b] = (best value, cargo) for exact budget usage <= b ; unbounded knapsack over capacity 40
    # state: capacity used 0..40, budget 0..BMAX
    NEG = -1
    dp = [[NEG]*(BMAX+1) for _ in range(CAP+1)]
    dp[0][0] = 0
    par = [[None]*(BMAX+1) for _ in range(CAP+1)]
    for i in range(4):
        ndp = [row[:] for row in dp]
        npar = [row[:] for row in par]
        for k in range(CAP+1):
            row = dp[k]; nrow = ndp[k+1] if k+1 <= CAP else None
            for b in range(BMAX+1):
                v = row[b]
                if v < 0: continue
                nb = b + p[i]
                if nb > BMAX: continue
                nv = v + w[i]
                if nv > nrow[nb]:
                    nrow[nb] = nv
                    npar[k+1][nb] = (i, k, b)
        dp, par = ndp, npar
    # best over capacity 0..40 and budget <= B
    best = [(NEG, None) for _ in range(BMAX+1)]
    runv, runc = NEG, None
    for B in range(BMAX+1):
        for k in range(CAP+1):
            v = dp[k][B]
            if v > runv:
                runv, runk, runB = v, k, B
        # reconstruct cargo for (runk, runB)
        c = [0]*4; k, b = runk, B
        while True:
            pr = par[k][b]
            if pr is None: break
            i, k0, b0 = pr
            c[i] += 1
            k, b = k0, b0
        best[B] = (runv, tuple(c))
        # prefix max already encoded since we scan k per B; but need max over budgets too -> do separately
    # now prefix over budgets
    prevv, prevc = NEG, None
    out = [None]*(BMAX+1)
    for B in range(BMAX+1):
        v, c = best[B]
        if v > prevv:
            prevv, prevc = v, c
        out[B] = (prevv, prevc)
    pre[t] = out

state = {("Fennick",(0,0,0,0)): 250}
for d in range(1, 8):
    newstate = {}
    for (t, c), gold in state.items():
        p = [WORLD["prices"][t][g] for g in GOODS]
        credit = gold + sum(p[i]*c[i] for i in range(4))
        B = min(credit, BMAX)
        val, c1 = pre[t][B]
        # val = sum w_i c1_i ; gold1 = gold + sum p_i c_i - sum p_i c1_i
        cost = sum(p[i]*c1[i] for i in range(4))
        g1 = gold + sum(p[i]*c[i] for i in range(4)) - cost
        if d == 7:
            # no travel; final: sell everything at local prices
            final = g1 + sum(p[i]*c1[i] for i in range(4))
            newstate[("END",)] = max(newstate.get(("END",), -1), final)
        else:
            for t2 in TOWNS:
                key = (t2, c1)
                if g1 > newstate.get(key, -1):
                    newstate[key] = g1
    state = newstate
    print("day", d, "states:", len(state), "max gold:", max(g for g in state.values()))
print("EXACT FINAL MAX GOLD:", max(state.values()))
EOF

So per state, we only need the argmax of that value, and among those, the one with the highest gold. This is the knapsack per source state I did in solve3 — but solve3 only considered candidates (single item / pair fill). The argmax of g1 + Σ M_i c1_i = gold + Σ p_i c_i + Σ c1_i (M_i - p_i) — this is an unbounded knapsack maximizing Σ c1_i w_i under capacity 40 and net expenditure ≤ gold, where w_i = M_i - p_i (which can be negative for some items in some towns: e.g., in Dunmere, w for timber = 0, w for salt = 0; in Fennick, w for spices/fish = 0).

w_i ≥ 0 always holds (M ≥ any price). So it's an unbounded knapsack: max Σ w_i c_i, Σ c_i ≤ 40, cost = Σ p_i c_i with "credit" = gold + Σ p_i c_i (the sell revenue of current cargo).
